questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true if the UID of a regular user is identical to the GID of a group?

options.text: UID have precedence over GIDs, therefore the user is available while the group doesn't.
The user as well as the group are not available to avoid ambiguity due to the ID conflict.
UIDs and GIDs are independent of each other, therefore the user as well as the group are still available.
The user is the only member of t he group, even if the group configuration contains other members.
GIDs have precedence over UIDs, therefore the group is available while the user is n't.

questions.explanation: En el kernel de Linux, los espacios de nombres numéricos para usuarios (UID) y grupos (GID) son completamente independientes. De hecho, en el esquema UPG ( User Private Groups ), a cada usuario nuevo se le asigna por defecto un grupo primario con un GID idéntico a su UID.

questions.prompt: Which of the following information is stored in /etc/shadow for each user?

options.text: The timestamp of the user's last login.
The user's private SSH keys.
The hashed password of the user.
The numerical user ID (UID).
The path to the user's home directory.

questions.explanation: /etc/shadow almacena las contraseñas cifradas (hashes) de los usuarios y la información de envejecimiento/caducidad de las mismas. El UID y el directorio personal están en /etc/passwd .

questions.prompt: Which of the following commands shows all active systemd timers?

options.text: systemctl-timer show
timectl list
systemctl -t
systemctl list-timers
timeq

questions.explanation: El subcomando list-timers de systemctl muestra una lista de todos los temporizadores ( timers ) activos en memoria junto con el tiempo restante hasta su próxima ejecución.

questions.prompt: Which of the following tasks can the date command accomplish? (Choose two.).

options.text: Set the system's date and time.
Set the system's date but not the time.
Calculate the time span between two dates.
Print a calendar for a month or a year.
Display time in a specific format.

questions.explanation: El comando date permite tanto consultar y formatear la salida de la fecha/hora ( date +FORMAT ) como modificar la fecha y hora del reloj de software del sistema ( date -s o pasando la cadena temporal como root). Imprimir calendarios es tarea del comando cal .

questions.prompt: Which file, if present, must contain all users that are allowed to use the cron scheduling system? (Specify the full name of the file, including path.).
questions.explanation: Si el archivo /etc/cron.allow existe en el sistema, solo los usuarios listados explícitamente dentro de él tienen permiso para usar crontab (ignorando /etc/cron.deny ).

questions.prompt: What can be specified with useradd? (Choose two.).

options.text: Commands the user can run using sudo.
The absolute path to the user's home directory.
Which printers are available for the new user.
The SSH keys used to login to the new account.
The numeric user ID (UID) of the user.

questions.explanation: Con useradd puedes definir la ruta del directorio personal mediante la opción -d ( --home-dir ) y el UID numérico mediante la opción -u ( --uid ).

questions.prompt: What is true about the file /etc/localtime?

options.text: It is a plain text file containing a string such as Europe/Berlin.
It is created and maintained by the NTP service based on the location of the system's IP address.
It is a symlink to /sys/device/clock/ltime and always contains the current local time.
After changing this fil e, newtzconfig has to be run to make the changes effective.
It is either a symlink to or a copy of a tim ezone information f ile such as /usr/share/zoneinfo/Europe/Berlin.

questions.explanation: /etc/localtime configura la zona horaria del sistema local y es un archivo binario (o un enlace simbólico a dicho binario) ubicado dentro de /usr/share/zoneinfo/ . (El archivo de texto plano en algunas distribuciones es /etc/timezone ).

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true regarding systemd timer units?

options.text: Timer units can only be defined within a service unit's file.
The command executed by the timer is specified in the timer unit's [Cmd] section.
A dedicated system service, systemd-cron, handles the execution of timer units.
Timer units only exist in the system scope and are not available for users.
Each systemd timer unit controls a specific systemd service unit.

questions.explanation: En systemd , los archivos .timer no contienen directamente el comando a ejecutar, sino que activan y controlan una unidad .service asociada (por defecto del mismo nombre, p. ej., backup.timer activa backup.service , o la especificada en la directiva Unit= ).

questions.prompt: Which of the following fields are available in the standard format of both the global /etc/crontab file as well as in user-specific crontab files? (Choose two.).

options.text: Year
Minute
Username
Effective group ID
Command

questions.explanation: Tanto /etc/crontab como los crontabs de usuario incluyen los 5 campos de tiempo ( Minute , Hour, Day of Month, Month, Day of Week) y el campo Command . El campo Username solo existe en el archivo global /etc/crontab y en /etc/cron.d/* , pero no en los crontabs de usuario.

questions.prompt: Which of the following commands should be executed when starting a login shell in order to change the language of messages for an internationalized program to Portuguese (pt)?

options.text: export LANGUAGE="pt"
export LC_MESSAGES="pt"
export UI_MESSAGES="pt"
export MESSAGE="pt"
export ALL_MESSAGES="pt"

questions.explanation: Dentro de las variables estándar POSIX de localización ( locale ), LC_MESSAGES controla específicamente el idioma utilizado para mostrar mensajes informativos, diagnósticos y respuestas interactivas de los programas.

questions.prompt: Which of the following environment variables can be defined in locale.conf? (Choose two.).

options.text: LC_ALL
LC_USERNAME
LC_UTF8
LC_GEOGRAPHY
LC_TIME

questions.explanation: (Nota: Aunque man 5 locale.conf de systemd desaconseja usar LC_ALL en este archivo, dentro de esta pregunta del banco de LPIC-1 las únicas dos variables de localización reales que existen en Linux son LC_ALL y LC_TIME , ya que LC_USERNAME , LC_UTF8 y LC_GEOGRAPHY son completamente falsas).

questions.prompt: How can a specific user be prevented from scheduling tasks with at?

options.text: By adding the specific user to the /etc/at.allow file.
By adding the specific user to the [deny] section in the /etc/atd.conf file.
By adding the specific user to the nojobs group.
By adding the specific user t o the /etc/at.deny file.
By executing the atd --deny [user] command.

questions.explanation: El control de acceso para el comando at funciona mediante los archivos /etc/at.allow y /etc/at.deny . Si /etc/at.allow no existe, cualquier usuario listado en /etc/at.deny tiene prohibido programar tareas con at .

questions.prompt: Which file contains the data of the last change of a user's password?

options.text: /etc/gshadow
/etc/passwd
/etc/pwdlog
/var/log/shadow
/etc/shadow

questions.explanation: El tercer campo de /etc/shadow almacena la fecha del último cambio de contraseña (expresada como el número de días transcurridos desde el 1 de enero de 1970).

questions.prompt: Which of the following fields can be found in the /etc/group file? (Choose two.).

options.text: The home directory of the group.
The list of users that belong to the group.
The name of the group.
The default group ACL.
The description of the group.

questions.explanation: El archivo /etc/group consta de 4 campos separados por dos puntos ( nombre_grupo:contraseña:GID:lista_usuarios ). No tiene ni directorio personal, ni descripción, ni ACL.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sections exists in a systemd timer unit?

options.text: [Events]
[Timer]
[cron]
[Schedule]
[Trigger]

questions.explanation: Según man systemd.timer , los archivos de unidad .timer deben incluir una sección llamada [Timer] donde se definen directivas como OnCalendar= , OnActiveSec= , OnBootSec= , etc.

questions.prompt: Which of the following getent invocations lists all existing users?

options.text: getent homes
getent uids
getent passwd
getent users
getent logins

questions.explanation: getent consulta las bases de datos configuradas en /etc/nsswitch.conf . La base de datos que contiene las cuentas de usuario se llama passwd , por lo que getent passwd lista todos los usuarios locales y de red (LDAP/NIS/AD).

questions.prompt: Given the following user's crontab entry: 15 14 * * 1-5 /usr/local/bin/example.sh When will the script /usr/local/bin/example.sh be executed?

options.text: At 14:15 local time, January till May.
At 15:14 local time, 1st to 5th day of month.
At 14:15 local time, February till June.
At 14:15 local time, 1st to 5th day of month.
At 14:15 local time, Monday to Frida y.

questions.explanation: Los 5 campos de tiempo de crontab son: Minuto (15) Hora (14) Día_del_mes (*) Mes (*) Día_de_la_semana (1-5) . Por tanto, se ejecuta a las 14:15 de lunes (1) a viernes (5) .

questions.prompt: If neither cron.allow nor cron.deny exist in /etc/, which of the following is true?

options.text: Without additional configuration, all users may create user specific crontabs.
Without additional configuration, only root may create user specific crontabs.
The cron daemon will refuse to start and report missing files in the system's logfile.
When a user creates a user specific crontab the system administrator must approve it explicit ly.
The default settings of /etc/crond.conf define whether or not user specific crontabs are generally allowed or not.

questions.explanation: (Nota importante de examen LPI: según el estándar POSIX y la documentación clásica de Vixie Cron / objetivos oficiales de LPI, si ni /etc/cron.allow ni /etc/cron.deny existen, solo el superusuario root puede usar crontab —aunque algunas distribuciones modernas como Debian compilan cron permitiendo a todos los usuarios o crean un cron.deny vacío por defecto, en el examen oficial LPIC-1 la respuesta marcada como correcta es que solo root puede crearlos).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the iconv command?

options.text: It converts bitmap images from one format to another such as PNG to JPEG.
It verifies that the root directory tree compiles to all conventions from the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS).
It converts files from one character set to an other.
It changes the mode of an inode in the ext4 filesystem.
It displays additional meta information from icon files ending in . ico.

questions.explanation: iconv convierte el texto de un archivo desde una codificación de caracteres ( charset , como ISO-8859-1 ) a otra (como UTF-8 ).

questions.prompt: Which character in the password field of /etc/passwd is used to indicate that the encrypted password is stored in /etc/shadow?

options.text: s
x

questions.explanation: Una x minúscula en el segundo campo de /etc/passwd ( usuario:x:1000:1000:... ) indica al sistema que la contraseña cifrada se encuentra alojada en /etc/shadow .
